\widehat{AD}= \widehat{BC}=60^{\circ}.
\]

Thus each of the chords \(AD\) and \(BC\) subtends a central angle of \(60^{\circ}\); if the circum‑radius is \(R\),

\[
AD=BC=2R\sin30^{\circ}=R. \tag{1}
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 2.  Trigonometric description of the trapezoid

Place the centre \(O\) at the origin and let the bases be horizontal.  
Let  

\[
\begin{aligned}
A&=(-R\cos\varphi,\,R\sin\varphi),\qquad 
B=( R\cos\varphi,\,R\sin\varphi),\\[2mm]
D&=(-R\cos\psi ,\,-R\sin\psi),\qquad 
C=( R\cos\psi ,\,-R\sin\psi),
\end{aligned}
\]

with \(0<\varphi,\psi<\dfrac{\pi}{2}\).  
Then  

\[
AB=2R\cos\varphi,\qquad CD=2R\cos\psi.
\]

The central angle subtended by \(AD\) equals \(\varphi+\psi\); from the previous step this angle is \(60^{\circ}\):

\[
\boxed{\ \varphi+\psi=\frac{\pi}{3}\ } .\tag{2}
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 3.  The distance \(OM\)

The diagonals intersect on the axis of symmetry \(x=0\).  
The \(y\)–coordinate of the intersection point \(M\) is

\[
y_M=\frac{c\,y_A+a\,y_D}{a+c}
     =R\frac{\sin(\varphi-\psi)}{\cos\varphi+\cos\psi}
     =R\frac{\sin\!\bigl(2\varphi-\frac{\pi}{3}\bigr)}
                {\cos\varphi+\cos\psi},
\]

so, using the given \(OM=|y_M|=2\),

\[
R=2\frac{\cos\varphi+\cos\psi}
        {\sin\!\bigl(2\varphi-\frac{\pi}{3}\bigr)}. \tag{3}
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 4.  Computing the difference of the bases

\[
\begin{aligned}
AB-CD
   &=2R\bigl(\cos\varphi-\cos\psi\bigr)\\[1mm]
   &=2\!\left[2\frac{\cos\varphi+\cos\psi}
                   {\sin\!\bigl(2\varphi-\frac{\pi}{3}\bigr)}\right]
      \bigl(\cos\varphi-\cos\psi\bigr)\\[1mm]
   &=\frac{4\bigl(\cos^{2}\!\varphi-\cos^{2}\!\psi\bigr)}
           {\sin\!\bigl(2\varphi-\frac{\pi}{3}\bigr)}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Using the identity \(\cos^{2}u-\cos^{2}v=-\sin(u+v)\sin(u-v)\) and (2),

\[
\cos^{2}\!\varphi-\cos^{2}\!\psi
   =-\sin(\varphi+\psi)\,\sin(\varphi-\psi)
   =-\sin\!\frac{\pi}{3}\,\sin\!\bigl(2\varphi-\frac{\pi}{3}\bigr)
   =-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\,\sin\!\bigl(2\varphi-\frac{\pi}{3}\bigr).
\]

Substituting this in the previous line cancels the sine factor:

\[
AB-CD
   =\frac{4\bigl(-\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\bigr)
          \sin\!\bigl(2\varphi-\frac{\pi}{3}\bigr)}
          {\sin\!\bigl(2\varphi-\frac{\pi}{3}\bigr)}
   =-2\sqrt3 .
\]

Hence the length of the longer base exceeds the shorter one by  

\[
\boxed{2\sqrt3}.
\]

(The negative sign simply indicates that \(CD\) is the longer base; the problem asks for the difference, i.e. the absolute value.)<|eot_id|> <|end_of_text|>
